error_modes.label: Vertical separation below the leader's exhaust

texts.0: SP, due to a pitch reference taken from the leader's wingtip instead of the exhaust line, did not stack the aircraft in the prescribed close trail position slightly below the leader's exhaust. The vertical separation sank past 15 feet below the exhaust line during the pull of the modified Lazy 8 and on the following reversal the aircraft climbed above the exhaust plane into the leader's flight path. The IP took control and repositioned the aircraft in the cone.
texts.1: SP, due to a delayed pitch correction each time the leader unloaded, did not hold the stack slightly below the exhaust. Vertical separation opened to approximately 15 feet below the exhaust line, at the code 1 limit, and stayed there through the maneuver. The position was recovered only after repeated verbal direction from the IP to reduce the sink and re-acquire the exhaust reference.
texts.2: SP, due to a coarse pitch input at the entry of the Chandelle, did not keep the stack tight under the leader's exhaust. Vertical separation increased to roughly 10 feet below the exhaust line, between the code 3 and code 1 values, and the aircraft was never allowed above the exhaust plane. SP recognized the sink and returned to the prescribed stack without any IP input.
texts.3: SP maintained the close trail stack slightly below the leader's exhaust throughout the turns and precision maneuvers. Vertical separation stayed within 5 feet under the exhaust line and the aircraft was never flown above that plane. Pitch corrections were small, promptly applied and immediately stabilized.
texts.4: SP held the aircraft on the exhaust reference with negligible vertical excursion through every maneuver flown. Deviations below the exhaust line remained a small fraction of the permitted 5 feet and no correction was ever visible as a discrete input. The stack was reproduced identically on each repetition of the profile.
texts.marginal: SP kept the vertical stack inside standards but consistently worked the low edge, holding close to 5 feet below the leader's exhaust rather than tight under it. The trend was a slow sink through every sustained pull, absorbed by a late catch each time. SP is expected to set the exhaust reference earlier in the pull so the stack is held without the recurring recovery.

texts_at.0: SP flew close trail with the IP calling for the pitch reference to be taken from the exhaust line rather than the wingtip, since this reference has not yet been introduced independently. This happens because the pitch reference is still taken from the leader's wingtip at the entry rather than from the exhaust line itself. This is the level of assistance the Training Section still provides at this stage. SP is expected to set the exhaust reference at maneuver entry so the sink stays smaller.
texts_at.1: SP let vertical separation open to about 15 feet below the leader's exhaust, at the code 1 limit, before the stack was recovered. The sink reached that far because the pitch reference is still taken from the leader's wingtip at the entry rather than from the exhaust line itself. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to set the exhaust reference at maneuver entry so the sink stays smaller.
texts_at.2: SP let vertical separation open to about 10 feet below the leader's exhaust, between the code 3 and code 1 values, before the sink was recognized and the prescribed stack restored without any input. The sink reached that far because the pitch correction at the entry of the maneuver was coarser than needed. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to soften that pitch input so the sink stays smaller.
texts_at.3: SP kept vertical separation inside about 5 feet under the leader's exhaust throughout the turns and precision maneuvers, applying small pitch corrections promptly. The small excursion that did appear followed a pitch input that was fractionally coarse. The maneuver was flown to the standard the Training Section requires at this point. SP is expected to soften that input further so the small excursion stops appearing.

texts_above.1: SP let vertical separation open to about 15 feet below the leader's exhaust, at the code 1 limit, before the stack was recovered. This followed a verbal call from the IP. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus.
texts_above.2: SP recognized every sink below the exhaust line and held vertical separation to about 10 feet under it, comfortably inside the acceptable band, returning to the prescribed stack without any input. Setting the exhaust reference at maneuver entry, rather than recovering it during the pull, would keep even that margin smaller. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to good vertical stack discipline.
texts_above.3: SP maintained the close trail stack slightly below the leader's exhaust throughout the turns and precision maneuvers, with vertical separation held inside about 3 feet under the exhaust line and the aircraft never flown above that plane. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to very good vertical stack discipline.
texts_above.4: SP held the aircraft on the exhaust reference with negligible vertical excursion through every maneuver flown, with deviations below the exhaust line staying a small fraction of the permitted margin and the stack reproduced identically on each repetition. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to excellent vertical stack discipline.

error_modes.label: Longitudinal nose-tail separation in ship lengths

texts.0: SP, due to power reductions timed after the leader had already unloaded, did not maintain the prescribed 1 to 2 ship lengths of nose-tail separation. Longitudinal separation opened beyond 4 ship lengths in the vertical portion of the modified Barrel Roll and the close trail position was effectively lost. The IP took control to reposition the aircraft on the leader before the maneuver could be continued.
texts.1: SP, due to a fixed power setting carried through the maneuver, did not adjust nose-tail separation to the leader's changing energy state. Longitudinal separation stabilized in the 3 to 4 ship length band, outside the prescribed position, and SP corrected it only after the IP called the aft drift twice. The closure back to position was slow and the correct spacing was not held for the rest of the maneuver.
texts.2: SP, due to a late power addition over the top of the modified Lazy 8, allowed the nose-tail spacing to open to about 3.5 ship lengths, beyond the prescribed close trail band. SP identified the aft drift on the descending line and closed back to about 3 ship lengths with a timely throttle input. No IP intervention or verbal prompt was required.
texts.3: SP held nose-tail separation between 1 and 2 ship lengths throughout the turns and precision maneuvers, as required for close trail. Spacing never opened past 2 ship lengths and never closed inside 1. Throttle inputs were anticipated so that the position was maintained rather than repeatedly regained.
texts.4: SP held the aircraft essentially fixed at about 1.5 ship lengths of nose-tail separation for the whole sequence. Spacing excursions were barely perceptible and were arrested before they developed into a closure or an opening rate. The same spacing was reproduced across turns, the modified Lazy 8 and the modified Barrel Roll without variation.
texts.marginal: SP stayed inside the 1 to 2 ship length band but consistently sat at the aft edge, close to 2 ship lengths, particularly in the second half of each maneuver. The tendency was to lose ground during the pull and regain it on the unload rather than hold a steady spacing. SP is expected to anticipate the power requirement at maneuver entry so the aft edge is not used as the working position.

texts_at.0: SP flew close trail with the IP calling for power to be adjusted to the leader's changing energy state, since holding nose-tail spacing through these maneuvers has not yet been practiced independently. This happens because the power setting is still held fixed through the maneuver rather than adjusted to the leader's changing energy state. The maneuver is being introduced at this point of the syllabus, so no independent standard is required yet. SP is expected to adjust power to the leader's energy state so the drift stays smaller.
texts_at.1: SP let nose-tail separation settle in the 3 to 4 ship length band, outside the prescribed position, before the aft drift was corrected. The spacing opened that far because the power setting is still held fixed through the maneuver rather than adjusted to the leader's changing energy state. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to adjust power to the leader's energy state so the drift stays smaller.
texts_at.2: SP let nose-tail spacing grow to about 3 ship lengths, beyond the prescribed band but short of the code 1 limit, before the aft drift was identified on the descending line and closed with a timely throttle input. The spacing grew that far because the power addition over the top lagged the leader's energy change. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to anticipate the power requirement at the top of the maneuver so the drift stays smaller.
texts_at.3: SP held nose-tail separation between 1 and 2 ship lengths throughout the turns and precision maneuvers, anticipating throttle inputs so the position was maintained rather than repeatedly regained. The small variation that did appear followed a throttle input that was fractionally late. The maneuver was flown to the standard the Training Section requires at this point. SP is expected to apply that input a fraction earlier so the small variation stops appearing.

texts_above.1: SP let nose-tail separation settle in the 3 to 4 ship length band, outside the prescribed position, before the aft drift was corrected. The correction came after a verbal call from the IP. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage of training.
texts_above.2: SP identified the aft drift on the descending line each time and closed nose-tail spacing to about 3 ship lengths, comfortably inside the acceptable band, with a timely throttle input and no further correction needed. Anticipating the power requirement at maneuver entry, rather than at the drift it produces, would keep even that margin smaller. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to sound nose-tail spacing control.
texts_above.3: SP held nose-tail separation between 1 and 2 ship lengths throughout the turns and precision maneuvers, as required for close trail, with spacing never opening past 2 ship lengths and throttle inputs anticipated so the position was maintained rather than repeatedly regained. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to sure-handed nose-tail spacing control.
texts_above.4: SP held the aircraft essentially fixed at about 1.5 ship lengths of nose-tail separation for the whole sequence, with spacing excursions barely perceptible and the same spacing reproduced across turns, the modified Lazy 8 and the modified Barrel Roll without variation. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to exceptional nose-tail spacing control.

error_modes.label: Minimum separation and closure control toward the leader

texts.0: SP, due to a perceptual error in judging closure against the leader's planform, did not respect the minimum of 1 ship length that must never be flown inside. Nose-tail separation reduced below 1 ship length with a positive closure rate as the leader unloaded at the top of the Chandelle. The IP took control and moved the aircraft out of the cone to stop the overtake.
texts.1: SP, due to a perceptual error in reading closure rate at high nose attitude, did not arrest the overtake toward the leader in time. Nose-tail separation reduced to about 1 ship length, on the minimum that must never be flown inside, and remained there while the closure was only slowly checked. Separation was re-established after the IP directed a power reduction and a lateral displacement out of the exhaust.
texts.2: SP, due to a misjudged closure cue as the leader's bank increased, allowed a noticeable overtake to develop toward the minimum separation. The gap reduced toward 1 ship length but SP recognized the closure rate early, reduced power and displaced slightly out of plane to stop the overtake. Separation was restored inside the prescribed band without IP intervention.
texts.3: SP controlled closure toward the leader accurately throughout the sortie and never flew inside 1 ship length. Overtake tendencies were recognized at onset and stopped with small power and out-of-plane corrections. The minimum separation was protected at every energy change of the leader.
texts.4: SP kept closure under precise control at all times, with no perceptible overtake toward the minimum separation on any maneuver. Corrections were anticipatory rather than reactive, so the gap never trended toward 1 ship length. Separation discipline was maintained equally in the turns and in the vertical portions of the profile.
texts.marginal: SP never flew inside 1 ship length but repeatedly closed to just outside it before checking the overtake. Corrections were made in time yet consistently at the last available point, leaving little margin at the leader's unload. SP is expected to recognize the closure cue earlier so the minimum separation is protected with a working margin rather than by a late catch.

texts_at.0: SP flew close trail with the IP calling the closure cue at high nose attitude as the leader's energy changed, since reading this cue has not yet been practiced independently. This happens because the closure cue at high nose attitude is still read late relative to the leader's energy change. Performance is consistent with a first exposure at this point of the syllabus, where the Training Section still provides assistance. SP is expected to read the closure cue earlier at high nose attitude so the margin above the minimum stays larger.
texts_at.1: SP let nose-tail separation close to the 1 ship length inner limit of the close trail position before the overtake was checked. The gap thinned that far because the closure cue at high nose attitude is still read late relative to the leader's energy change. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to read the closure cue earlier at high nose attitude so the margin above the minimum stays larger.
texts_at.2: SP let nose-tail separation close toward the 1 ship length inner limit before the closure rate was recognized early and stopped with a reduction in power and a small displacement out of plane. The gap thinned that far because the closure cue as the leader's bank increased was misjudged by a small amount. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to assess that cue before the bank increases rather than as it does.
texts_at.3: SP controlled closure toward the leader accurately throughout the sortie, never flying inside about 1.7 ship lengths, with overtake tendencies recognized at onset and stopped with small power and out-of-plane corrections. The small reduction that did appear followed a recognition that was a beat later than ideal. The maneuver was flown to the standard the Training Section requires at this point. SP is expected to recognize that cue a beat earlier so the small reduction stops appearing.

texts_above.1: SP let nose-tail separation close to the 1 ship length inner limit of the close trail position before the overtake was checked. The correction followed a verbal call from the IP. This is above the level the Training Section requires at this point.
texts_above.2: SP recognized the closure rate early on every occasion and held the gap clear of the 1 ship length inner limit, stopping it with a power reduction and a small displacement out of plane. Assessing the closure cue before the bank increases, rather than as it does, would keep even that margin more comfortable. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to steady closure discipline.
texts_above.3: SP controlled closure toward the leader accurately throughout the sortie and never flew inside about 1.7 ship lengths, with overtake tendencies recognized at onset and stopped with small power and out-of-plane corrections at every energy change of the leader. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to consistently accurate closure discipline.
texts_above.4: SP kept closure under precise control at all times, with no perceptible overtake toward the minimum separation on any maneuver, since corrections were anticipatory rather than reactive in both the turns and the vertical portions of the profile. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to exemplary closure discipline.

error_modes.label: As Leader: smoothness and positive-G through the maneuvers

texts.0: SP, due to an abrupt stick reversal at the apex of the modified Barrel Roll, did not carry out the maneuver smoothly with positive G maintained at all times. The aircraft was unloaded to zero and below while flown as leader, which is not permitted with No 2 in close trail, and the resulting flight path change was unpredictable for the wingman. The IP took control to restore a positive-G flight path and stop the maneuver.
texts.1: SP, due to uncoordinated pitch and roll inputs, did not fly the precision maneuvers with the smoothness required of the leader. G loading was allowed to fall to near zero over the top of the modified Lazy 8 and the flight path became step-shaped rather than continuous. Smooth positive-G flight was restored only after the IP verbally directed a continuous pull, and the same input pattern reappeared on the next repetition.
texts.2: SP, due to a rushed roll input at the entry, did not maintain a fully smooth positive-G flight path as leader. G loading dropped noticeably in the first third of the modified Barrel Roll, though it stayed positive throughout. SP recognized the discontinuity, blended the pull and completed the remainder of the maneuver smoothly without any IP input.
texts.3: SP flew the turns, the modified Lazy 8, the Chandelle and the modified Barrel Rolls smoothly as leader, with positive G maintained at all times. Pitch and roll inputs were blended so the flight path remained continuous and predictable for the aircraft in close trail. No abrupt reversals or unloading occurred at any point of the profile.
texts.4: SP produced a flight path of consistently high quality as leader, with G loading held smoothly positive and free of any perceptible step. Entries, apexes and recoveries were blended so that the wingman's position requirement never changed abruptly. The quality of the flight path was identical on every repetition of the profile.
texts.marginal: SP kept the flight path smooth and positive-G within standards but allowed the loading to become light at each apex before the pull was re-established. The maneuvers were acceptable yet the transitions were the weakest part of each one. SP is expected to carry a more continuous pull through the apex so the flight path presented to the wingman does not soften at the top.

texts_at.0: SP flew as leader with the IP calling for pitch and roll to be blended into one continuous pull, since this smoothness has not yet been practiced independently. This happens because pitch and roll inputs are still applied separately rather than blended into one continuous pull. The Training Section still expects IP assistance for this maneuver at this point. SP is expected to blend pitch and roll into one continuous pull so the loading sag stays smaller.
texts_at.1: SP let G loading sag to about 0.3 G over the top of the maneuver, close to unloaded, before smooth positive-G flight was restored. The loading sagged that far because pitch and roll inputs are still applied separately rather than blended into one continuous pull. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to blend pitch and roll into one continuous pull so the loading sag stays smaller.
texts_at.2: SP let G loading sag to about 0.6 G in the first third of the maneuver, staying positive throughout, before the discontinuity was recognized and the pull blended for the remainder of the maneuver. The loading sagged that far because the roll input at the entry was applied ahead of the pitch input rather than with it. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to enter the roll and the pull together so the loading sag stays smaller.
texts_at.3: SP flew the maneuvers smoothly as leader, with G loading held within about 0.2 G of a steady positive value, so the flight path remained continuous and predictable for the aircraft in close trail. The small variation that did appear followed a pull that eased fractionally at the apex. The maneuver was flown to the standard the Training Section requires at this point. SP is expected to carry that pull a fraction more continuously through the apex so the small variation stops appearing.

texts_above.1: SP let G loading sag to about 0.3 G over the top of the maneuver, close to unloaded, before smooth positive-G flight was restored. This followed a verbal call from the IP. The result is above the code required for this Training Section at this stage of training.
texts_above.2: SP recognized the loading discontinuity at the entry and held G within about 0.6 G of steady, comfortably positive throughout, blending the pull for the remainder of the maneuver without any input from the IP. Entering the roll and the pull together, rather than the roll first, would keep even that margin smaller. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to dependable flight-path smoothness as leader.
texts_above.3: SP flew the turns, the modified Lazy 8, the Chandelle and the modified Barrel Rolls smoothly as leader, with positive G held within about 0.2 G of a steady value and pitch and roll inputs blended so the flight path remained continuous and predictable for the aircraft in close trail. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to notably good flight-path smoothness as leader.
texts_above.4: SP produced a flight path of consistently high quality as leader, with G loading held smoothly positive and free of any perceptible step, so entries, apexes and recoveries were blended and the wingman's position requirement never changed abruptly. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to superior flight-path smoothness as leader.

error_modes.label: As Leader: airspeed, G and bank limits during the maneuvers

texts.0: SP, due to an entry flown with excess energy and no compensating power reduction, did not keep the maneuvers inside the airspeed range of 120 to 250 KIAS and the applicable limits. Airspeed exceeded 250 KIAS on the recovery from the modified Lazy 8 and the pull was carried past 3 G with the wingman in close trail. The IP took control to unload the aircraft and reset the parameters.
texts.1: SP, due to power not being repositioned before the descending line, did not hold the airspeed inside the range required as leader. Airspeed reached approximately 250 KIAS at the recovery and bank was carried to the 90 degree maximum with no margin. Both parameters were brought back only after the IP called them, and the entry parameters for the next maneuver were again not set.
texts.2: SP, due to a late power reduction on the descending line, allowed airspeed to increase toward the upper end of the permitted range. The value stabilized in the low 200s KIAS, above the intended entry parameter but well inside 250 KIAS. SP recognized the trend, reduced power and re-established the briefed entry airspeed without any IP input.
texts.3: SP flew the turns and precision maneuvers as leader within the airspeed range of 120 to 250 KIAS and within the maneuver limits of 3 G and 90 degrees of bank. Power was repositioned ahead of each energy change so the parameters were set rather than recovered. Entry and recovery airspeeds were repeatable across the profile.
texts.4: SP controlled energy so precisely that airspeed remained well inside the 120 to 250 KIAS range on every entry, apex and recovery. G and bank were held comfortably below the applicable maxima with margin retained throughout. The same entry parameters were reproduced on each maneuver without visible correction.
texts.marginal: SP remained inside the airspeed range and maneuver limits but repeatedly used the upper part of the band, arriving near 240 KIAS at each recovery. The margin to 250 KIAS was thin and was preserved by a late power reduction rather than by planned energy management. SP is expected to set the recovery power earlier so the upper limit is approached with a deliberate margin.

texts_at.0: SP flew as leader with the IP calling for power to be repositioned before the recovery, since managing these limits has not yet been practiced independently. This happens because the power reposition for the next maneuver is still made after the recovery rather than before it. The Training Section introduces this maneuver at this point and does not yet ask for an independent standard. SP is expected to reposition power before the recovery so the margin to the boundary stays larger.
texts_at.1: SP let airspeed reach about 245 KIAS at the recovery, close to the 250 KIAS boundary, and carried bank close to the 90 degree maximum before the parameters were brought back. The margin thinned that far because the power reposition for the next maneuver is still made after the recovery rather than before it. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to reposition power before the recovery so the margin to the boundary stays larger.
texts_at.2: SP let airspeed reach about 230 KIAS at the recovery, above the intended entry parameter but inside the 250 KIAS limit, before the trend was recognized and power reduced to re-establish the briefed entry airspeed without any input. The margin thinned that far because the power reduction on the descending line was applied later than ideal. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to reduce power a moment earlier on the descending line so the margin stays larger.
texts_at.3: SP flew the turns and precision maneuvers as leader within the airspeed range of 120 to 250 KIAS and within the maneuver limits of 3 G and 90 degrees of bank, repositioning power ahead of each energy change so entry and recovery airspeeds stayed near 200 KIAS and repeatable. The small variation that did appear followed a repositioning that was a fraction later than ideal. The maneuver was flown to the standard the Training Section requires at this point. SP is expected to reposition power a fraction earlier so the small variation stops appearing.

texts_above.1: SP let airspeed reach about 245 KIAS at the recovery, close to the 250 KIAS boundary, and carried bank close to the 90 degree maximum before the parameters were brought back. The correction came after a verbal call from the IP. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus.
texts_above.2: SP recognized the airspeed trend on the descending line each time and held recovery airspeed to about 230 KIAS, comfortably inside the 250 KIAS limit, re-establishing the briefed entry airspeed without any input. Repositioning power before the recovery, rather than after it, would keep even that margin larger. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to assured energy-limit management as leader.
texts_above.3: SP flew the turns and precision maneuvers as leader within the airspeed range of 120 to 250 KIAS and within the maneuver limits of 3 G and 90 degrees of bank, with power repositioned ahead of each energy change so entry and recovery airspeeds near 200 KIAS were repeatable across the profile. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to precise energy-limit management as leader.
texts_above.4: SP controlled energy so precisely that airspeed remained well inside the 120 to 250 KIAS range on every entry, apex and recovery, with G and bank held comfortably below the applicable maxima and margin retained throughout. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to first-rate energy-limit management as leader.

error_modes.label: As Leader: orientation within the assigned flight area

texts.0: SP, due to lack of awareness of the aircraft's position relative to the area boundary, did not maintain orientation within the assigned flight area while leading the maneuvers. Successive modified Barrel Rolls were flown in the same direction without any repositioning turn and the formation left the working area. The IP took control to return the formation inside the assigned airspace.
texts.1: SP, due to lack of awareness of the ground reference used for area orientation, did not manage the position of the formation within the assigned flight area. The aircraft arrived within a very short distance of the boundary with no repositioning planned, and the turn back was flown only after the IP stated the position. Area orientation for the following maneuver was again not established before entry.
texts.2: SP, due to attention concentrated on the maneuver parameters at the expense of area orientation, allowed the formation to work toward one side of the assigned flight area. SP identified the drift on the recovery from the Chandelle and repositioned with a turn back toward the center of the area before the boundary became a factor. No IP prompting was required.
texts.3: SP maintained orientation within the assigned flight area throughout the sortie while leading the maneuvers. Entry headings were selected so that each maneuver kept the formation inside the working airspace and repositioning turns were flown when required. Area position was known at all times and never became a limiting factor.
texts.4: SP managed the geometry of the working area precisely, keeping the formation centered in the assigned airspace for the whole sequence. Maneuver entry headings were planned in advance so that no corrective repositioning was ever needed. Awareness of the boundaries was evident without any interruption to the quality of the maneuvers.
texts.marginal: SP kept the formation inside the assigned flight area but used the outer third of it, repositioning only when the boundary was already close. Area management was correct in outcome yet reactive in method. SP is expected to plan entry headings so the maneuvers are flown from the center of the area rather than toward its edge.

texts_at.0: SP flew as leader with the IP calling out the formation's position against the area boundary, since maintaining a continuously updated position picture has not yet been practiced independently. This happens because the ground reference used for area orientation is still a single feature rather than a continuously updated position. This is the level of assistance the Training Section still provides at this stage. SP is expected to update the position picture continuously so the margin to the boundary stays larger.
texts_at.1: SP let the formation come within about half a mile of the area boundary, with no repositioning planned, before the turn back was flown after the position was stated. The margin thinned that far because the ground reference used for area orientation is still a single feature rather than a continuously updated position. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to update the position picture continuously so the margin to the boundary stays larger.
texts_at.2: SP let the formation work to about a mile from the area boundary, off-center in the working airspace, before the drift was identified on the recovery from a maneuver and repositioned toward the center without prompting. The margin thinned that far because attention was concentrated on the maneuver parameters rather than area orientation. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to check area position between maneuvers rather than only when the boundary becomes close.
texts_at.3: SP maintained orientation within the assigned flight area throughout the sortie, keeping the formation with several miles of margin on every side by selecting entry headings that kept each maneuver inside the working airspace. The small reduction in margin that did appear followed an entry heading that was a fraction less central than ideal. The maneuver was flown to the standard the Training Section requires at this point. SP is expected to select that heading a fraction more centrally so the small reduction stops appearing.

texts_above.1: SP let the formation come within about half a mile of the area boundary, with no repositioning planned, before the turn back was flown after the position was stated. The correction followed a verbal call from the IP. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage of training.
texts_above.2: SP identified the drift toward one side of the area without prompting and repositioned the formation to about a mile of margin from the boundary, comfortably inside the working airspace, with no IP prompting required. Checking area position between maneuvers, rather than only when the boundary becomes close, would keep even that margin more comfortable. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to steady area-orientation management as leader.
texts_above.3: SP maintained orientation within the assigned flight area throughout the sortie while leading the maneuvers, selecting entry headings that kept the formation with several miles of margin inside the working airspace and repositioning when required. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to consistently accurate area-orientation management as leader.

This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to exemplary area-orientation management as leader.

error_modes.label: As Wingman: power anticipation and energy management in the cone

texts.0: SP, due to throttle inputs made only after the position had already changed, did not maintain the close trail position through the leader's energy changes. Power was repeatedly moved to the stops, producing alternating overtake and aft drift that left the aircraft outside the cone for most of the maneuver. The IP took control and re-established the position on the leader.
texts.1: SP, due to reliance on visual size cues alone with no anticipation of the leader's pull, did not manage energy to hold the close trail position. Power lagged each entry and recovery, so the aircraft arrived at the limit of the permitted position on every maneuver and was held there. Correct energy management was applied only after the IP directed the power to be set before the entry, and the technique was not carried into the next repetition.
texts.2: SP, due to a power addition applied at the apex rather than during the pull, did not hold the close trail position steadily through the vertical portion of the modified Lazy 8. The aircraft drifted noticeably aft and low before the correction took effect, remaining short of the code 1 values. SP recognized the pattern, moved the power earlier on the following maneuver and held position without IP input.
texts.3: SP anticipated the leader's energy changes and set power before each entry, apex and recovery. The close trail position was maintained through the turns and precision maneuvers with small, early throttle corrections rather than large late ones. Position was held rather than repeatedly regained.
texts.4: SP managed energy so accurately that the close trail position appeared static through the whole profile. Power was repositioned continuously and in small increments in step with the leader, and no corrective excursion in spacing or stack was observable. The technique was applied identically in the turns and in the modified Barrel Rolls.
texts.marginal: SP held the close trail position within standards but with power corrections that were consistently larger and later than necessary. Position was maintained by a series of catches rather than by anticipation, which left the technique dependent on a quick recovery. SP is expected to move the power at the leader's input rather than at the first visible change of position.

texts_at.0: SP flew as wingman with the IP calling for power to be set before the leader's pull, since anticipating this energy change has not yet been practiced independently. This happens because power still lags the leader's pull rather than being set before it. The maneuver is being introduced at this point of the syllabus, so no independent standard is required yet.
